subsection.title: Substitution
subsection.p: Substitution reverses the chain rule. A useful sufficient hypothesis for the definite formula is that g is continuously differentiable on [a,b] and f is continuous on an interval containing the range of g. No monotonicity of g is needed in this signed formula.

li.p: For definite integrals, change the limits.
For indefinite integrals, substitute back to x.

subsection.title: Warning
subsection.p: The substitution u=g(x) requires the matching factor g'(x)\,dx.
For example, \int 2x e^{x^2}\,dx is directly handled by u=x^2, but \int e^{x^2}\,dx is not.

subsection.title: Integration by parts
subsection.p: Integration by parts reverses the product rule. The definite formula applies to continuously differentiable functions u,v on [a,b], with du=u'(x)\,dx and dv=v'(x)\,dx.

subsection.title: Useful choices
subsection.p: For \int x e^x\,dx, take u=x,\qquad dv=e^x\,dx.
For \int x\cos x\,dx, take u=x,\qquad dv=\cos x\,dx.
For \int \ln x\,dx, take u=\ln x,\qquad dv=dx.

subsection.title: Warning
subsection.p: Integration by parts creates a boundary term: [uv]_a^b. Do not drop it.
